blocks.text:
Travel by bus to Yaxha National Park.

The television series "Survivor: Guatemala – The Maya Empire" was filmed here.

Yaxha means "blue-green water". The ancient city lies between two lagoons, Sacnab and Yaxha.

Its notable structures include the Royal Palace, where the ruler lived with his family, the North Acropolis, the Astronomical Complex, two ball courts, the East Acropolis, the Plaza of Shadows and the twin-pyramid complex.

Roads and paved passages connect the buildings. More than 500 structures have been found at Yaxha.

Walk along the causeways, through the plazas and temples, and learn about the history of this Maya city.

After lunch, travel to the Belize border, then transfer to Blancaneaux Lodge in the Pine Ridge Mountains.

The lodge lies within the Mountain Pine Ridge Forest Reserve. Guests have access to an outdoor pool, a garden growing organic produce and two restaurants.

The bungalows and villas overlook the river. There is an orchid-lined path on the grounds. On request, the lodge staff can help arrange walks to the nearby waterfall and caves.

blocks.text:
Today, you are in for an exciting tour! The first stop is at the pools and waterfalls, where guests can refresh themselves by swimming in the cool waters or relaxing in natural jacuzzis.

After this stop, we continue the excursion to the Caracol archaeological ruins.

The tour begins at the largest archaeological site in Belize, covering 30 square miles in the high canopy of the jungle, and includes five plazas, an astronomical observatory, and over 35,000 buildings. The ruins of the ancient city of Caracol, located on the Vaca Plateau, were discovered in 1936. The Canaa Pyramid is still one of the tallest structures in Belize (its height is 42 meters). Over 100 ceremonial tombs from the 6th to 8th centuries have revealed beautiful examples of hieroglyphic writing, telling the story of the war between Caracol and Tikal. In the surrounding forested excavations, tapirs, jaguars, ocelots, and thousands of birds, including rare orange-breasted falcons and harpy eagles, can often be spotted.
